sources.entry: go-doxy - Lightweight, simple, and performant reverse proxy with WebUI, Docker integration, automatic shutdown/startup for container based on traffic. MIT Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: GoDoxy is a lightweight reverse proxy with a WebUI that routes traffic to Docker and Podman containers, Proxmox nodes and LXC containers, with optional idle sleep for containers.
summary.what_it_does: GoDoxy lists running containers, reads their names, labels and port configuration, and creates routes (virtual-host style) automatically, watching for container and config changes to update them. Routes can also be defined with route files or Docker labels such as proxy.aliases for subdomains. It supports HTTP reverse proxying, TCP/UDP port forwarding, OpenID Connect SSO, ForwardAuth integration, HTTP middlewares and custom error pages. Access control includes IP/CIDR rules, country and timezone rules (using a MaxMind account), access logging and periodic summaries. A WebUI manages routes, config, containers, logs, metrics and uptime, and Let's Encrypt certificates can be issued through DNS-01 providers.
use_cases: reverse proxy for self-hosted Docker apps
sleep idle containers to save resources
wildcard domain proxying to home services
Proxmox LXC route binding and control
SSO and ForwardAuth in front of web apps
how_to_run: Configure a wildcard DNS record (e.g. *.domain.com) pointing to the machine running GoDoxy
Prepare a new directory for Docker Compose and config files
Run the setup script inside the directory, or set up manually
Manual setup: mkdir -p config && wget -O config/config.yml (from config.example.yml), then fetch .env.example and compose.example.yml
notable: Automatic route discovery from Docker/Podman labels with hot reload
Idle sleep that stops and wakes Docker and Proxmox LXC containers based on traffic
Proxmox integration with route binding and LXC start/stop/restart from the WebUI
Built-in WebUI for routes, logs, metrics and uptime
Ships an install/update/uninstall script supporting systemd and Alpine/OpenRC
caveats: Designed to run in Docker host network mode; the README says not to change it
Platform support listed as Linux amd64 and arm64 only
Country and timezone rules require a MaxMind account
